title: Canonically equivalent Unicode text can have different bytes
summary: Precomposed é and e followed by a combining acute accent compare equal after NFC normalization, but have different raw UTF-8 bytes.
applies: Unicode text and JSON byte records
detail: The former is C3 A9 and the latter is 65 CC 81. Hashing their raw bytes produces different digests.
boundary: NFKC also handles compatibility equivalence; the original bytes are preserved before normalizing the evidence.
relevance: Determine why password prompts, file names, or text that appear to be identical do not compare equal.
